CITY OF READING, OHIO
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES – LEGISLATIVE SESSION
AUGUST 18, 2026 – 7:30 PM 
For the full detail of this evening’s Council Meeting, please visit www.watchreadingohio.com . 
CALL TO ORDER 
President of Council, Mr. Mattscheck called the meeting to order at 7:30 PM. 
INVOCATION AND PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE 
President of Council, Mr. Mattscheck led those in attendance in a prayer and then the Pledge of Allegiance. 
ROLL CALL 
Council Members Present: Mr. Powell, Mr. Bronner, Mr. Bishop, Mr. Boehner, Mr. Thamann, Mrs. Kroeger,
& Mrs. Eadicicco. 
OTHER CITY OFFICIALS PRESENT: 
Mayor Bo Bemmes & Clerk of Council Carla Bronner 
APPROVAL OF MINUTES: Motion to approve the August 4, 2026, Council Meeting Minutes made by Mr. Boehner,
seconded by Mr. Bronner. Motion carried by voice vote. 
SWEARING IN CEREMONY 
Mayor Bo Bemmes performed the Oath of Office for Officer Rick Ellison, who was sworn in as Lieutenant 
GUEST SPEAKERS: NONE
AUDIENCE ASKING PARTICIPATION:
(1) Bob Ashbrock – Requested that Council table the proposed zoning-code ordinance, arguing that required public-hearing
notifications and procedural steps had not been properly completed. In response, Council indicated that the ordinance had gone
through committee and the Planning Commission and that the public hearing had been advertised, but agreed to verify the details
of the notification. 
READING OF COMMUNICATIONS: 
(1) July 2026 Mayor’s Court Monthly Disbursement Report 
121 Bench warrants Issued, 206 Cases Heard & $17,447.00 Collected 
LEGISLATIVE SESSION 
READING OF RESOLUTIONS: NONE
READING OF ORDINANCES:
(1) AN ORDINANCE ADOPTING CHANGES TO THE ZONING CODE. (Second Reading) 
Ordinance was declared a second reading only 
(2) AN ORDINANCE AUTHORIZING THE PURCHASE OF A 2027 FORD F-450 TRUCK FOR
AN AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $115,000.00 AND DECLARING AN EMERGENCY. 
Motion made by Mrs. Eadicicco, seconded by Mrs. Kroeger, to suspend the rule that requires a second & third reading.
Motion carried by a 7-0 roll call vote. Motion made by Mr. Bishop, seconded by Mrs. Eadicicco to adopt the
ordinance. Motion carried by a 7-0 roll call vote. 
ORDINANCE ADOPTED ORDINANCE NUMBER 2026-25 
MISCELLANEOUS BUSINESS:
(1) Bo Bemmes: 
Tonight it is an honor for me to administer the oath of office to Police Officer Rick Ellison as he becomes a Lieutenant for our

Page 2 08-18-2026 Reading Council Minutes 
outstanding Police Department. Rick is in his 26 th year as a member of our Police Department. I want to thank Rick and all of the
members of our PD for their willingness to serve our Community. 
Schools in our City are open so PLEASE SLOW DOWN AS YOU DRIVE AND KEEP AN EYE OUT FOR OUR YOUNG
STUDENTS AS THEY MAKE THEIR WAY TO AND FROM SCHOOL 
Our American Legion will be hosting a feed the community event in their parking lot on Saturday August 22 from noon till
5pm serving hot dogs, chips and bottled water. ALL ARE WELCOME 
The annual Taste of Reading will be held at Koenig Park from noon till 11pm on Saturday August 29 
Our Reading Bridal Association will hold their annual Fall in Love event on Benson Street on Thursday September 17. Benson
Street will be closed from 5pm till 10pm from Reading Road to Wachendorf 
Our Lady of the Valley’s festival will be held on September 18, 19 and 20 
87 events in 93 days are scheduled on Veterans Memorial Field 
We are accepting bids for the new track and fencing around the track and around Veterans Memorial Complex 
Please call me anytime with any City related questions, comments or concerns at 513-509-8619 
(2) Mark Bishop: Reported on the 15th anniversary celebration of Agape Love Ministries, a local church near Sunnybrook
Lane. He noted that the organization has grown significantly since it began in the pastor's basement in an apartment complex. 
Agape Love Ministries provides food, supplies, and other assistance to the community. Mr. Bishop represented the city at the
anniversary celebration and presented the organization with a proclamation recognizing its 15 years of service and success. 
He congratulated Pastor Dr. Cornelius Henderson Sr. and his wife, Pastor Michelle Henderson, and expressed his appreciation for
the opportunity to participate in the celebration. 
(3) Katie Eadicicco: Asked about the planned track replacement and whether the project would accommodate a potential future
expansion of the athletic field. She noted that one of the goals associated with the levy was to install turf and expand the field to
meet regulation size requirements. 
She asked whether reducing the track from eight lanes to six lanes was part of the plan in order to preserve space for a future field
expansion, while acknowledging that no field expansion is currently planned. 
It was confirmed that the track will be reduced to six lanes. Council also discussed previous track proposals and the possibility of
installing turf in the future. Two companies have indicated that a track can be installed before turf, although installing the turf first
would be preferable. 
The six-lane configuration is intended to preserve the necessary space and measurements should the city have an opportunity to
expand the field in the future. 
(4) Bob Boehner: 
This is a short version of our discussion of equipment needs and curb work on July 21, 2026: 
The Service Dept. is asking for a Hot Box Trailer to haul Blacktop to patch potholes. We decided to put this purchase off till
2027. 
We discussed purchasing 1 truck and that truck and snowplow equipment is estimated to cost $111,372.05. It will replace Truck
#25 and 
The new truck will be used for snow events in the alleys and narrow streets in the valley area. This price will be verified by the
Service Dept. prior to passing an Ordinance.

Page 3 08-18-2026 Reading Council Minutes 
We also pushed another truck purchase to 2027. This 5-ton vehicle is for multiple water main repairs, this will help get more
equipment to the water main site. 
Curb work was discussed to replace all curbs on Genoma, Wenchris would be the next in line. More curbs are missing or in
disrepair on Genoma. 
ADJOURNMENT 
Motion to adjourn came from Mr. Bishop, and was seconded by Mrs. Kroeger. Motion carried by voice vote. There
being no further business, the meeting was declared adjourned at 7:55 pm.
